newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan activists to stage protest against China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan activists to stage protest against China.

text.p: Taiwan independence advocates pledged on Wednesday to organise a 100,000-strong march just days ahead of Hong Kong's handover to China to oppose Beijing's call for their island's own reunification with the mainland.

"We will stage a huge march in Taipei on June 28, just two days before China retakes Hong Kong, to show our dissatisfaction over the communists' attempt to swallow Taiwan," said Taiwan Independence Party chairman Lee Chen-yuan.
Lee said 100,000 supporters would turn out for the "Say No to China" march through the capital's streets.
Party officials said the protest was needed to remind Taiwanese of their right to self-determination.
"We doubt very much that China will really allow Hong Kong to maintain its freedom of speech and decide its own future after the handover," a party official said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule. Beijing has promised to maintain Hong Kong's current system for at least 50 years.
Chiu Yi-jen, secretary-general of Taiwan's main opposition Democratic Progressive Party, said his party and several other groups would mobilise members for the march.

"We will make it clear that we will never accept China's 'one country, two system' proposal and will never believe that such a proposal can improve relations between the sides of the Taiwan strait," Chiu said.

Taiwan and China split after a civil war ended in 1949. Beijing, which views Taiwan as a rebel-held province, has warned the island against striving for independence, saying this would precipitate pre-emptive military strikes.
China has proposed the "one country, two systems" model to allow Taiwan and Hong Kong to maintain their capitalist systems -- albeit under the communist state's sovereignty.
